title: Haemonetics Cell Saver Elite+ Cell Salvage System - Air Detected in Aspiration Line or SmartSuction Is Unstable
description: Addresses aspiration-line air and unstable suction caused by loose connections, empty fluid sources, leaks, tubing position, occlusion, or suction-path problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Continuity of Care
steps.instructions: Do not rely on unstable aspiration or blood collection during an active case. Notify the clinical team and provide an alternate method of surgical suction or blood-management support as appropriate. Expected outcome: Required suction and patient care continue safely while the Cell Saver Elite+ is evaluated.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Symptom
steps.instructions: Determine whether visible air is entering the aspiration line, suction varies unexpectedly, suction stops and restarts, or the system repeatedly indicates an air-related condition. Observe the entire accessible aspiration path. Expected outcome: The condition is reproduced or localized to a specific part of the aspiration circuit.

steps.title: 3. Inspect All Aspiration-Line Connections
steps.instructions: Check tubing connections from the surgical field toward the reservoir and system. Look for loose fittings, partially inserted connectors, cracked tubing, or disconnected ports. Expected outcome: All external aspiration connections are secure and intact. If tightening or replacing an external connection eliminates air entry, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Tubing for Cracks, Kinks, and Collapse
steps.instructions: Trace the aspiration tubing for punctures, cuts, soft or collapsed sections, severe bends, or tubing compressed by equipment. Replace compromised disposable tubing as appropriate. Expected outcome: The aspiration line is intact and unobstructed.

steps.title: 5. Verify Associated Fluid and Suction Setup
steps.instructions: Check clinically managed fluid sources and suction accessories involved in the aspiration setup for empty containers, closed clamps, improper connection, or other obvious external conditions. Do not change clinical suction parameters without appropriate authorization. Expected outcome: External aspiration support components are correctly connected and available.

steps.title: 6. Check Reservoir and Disposable Connections
steps.instructions: Confirm reservoir ports and disposable connections are properly seated and not allowing air entry. Look for cracked ports, damaged seals, or improperly fitted tubing. Expected outcome: The reservoir and disposable path are secure. If correcting a connection stabilizes suction, the issue is resolved.

steps.title: 7. Evaluate Aspiration-Line Positioning
steps.instructions: Observe whether tubing is sharply elevated, dependent, compressed, or positioned in a way that promotes intermittent flow or air entrainment. Reposition external tubing without disturbing the sterile field. Expected outcome: Tubing routing supports stable aspiration without mechanical restriction.

steps.title: 8. Compare With Known-Good Disposable Components
steps.instructions: When appropriate, substitute a known-good compatible aspiration line or relevant disposable component to determine whether the instability follows the disposable. Expected outcome: Stable suction with a known-good disposable indicates the original component was the likely cause.

steps.title: 9. Perform Nonpatient Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Using an appropriate setup, verify that suction remains stable and that air is not being drawn into the fluid path from external connections. Expected outcome: Aspiration remains stable without unexplained air entry. Troubleshooting can stop if the test passes consistently.

steps.title: 10. Remove From Service if Suction Control Remains Unstable
steps.instructions: If all external tubing, connections, disposables, and setup conditions are verified but suction remains unstable, remove the system from service. Label it Out of Service and send it for service-level evaluation. Expected outcome: An unreliable aspiration system is prevented from returning to clinical use.

CCR.Complaint: OR staff reported visible air entering the aspiration tubing and unstable suction during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a loose aspiration-line connection at the reservoir that was allowing air into the circuit.
CCR.Resolution: The connection was secured, and functional testing confirmed stable aspiration without visible air entry.

helpfulDetails: Suction behavior before and after correction

title: Haemonetics Cell Saver Elite+ Cell Salvage System - Barcode, USB, Ethernet, or Wi-Fi Data Transfer Failure
description: Addresses barcode and data-transfer failures caused by accessories, cables, media, network availability, configuration, signal conditions, or infrastructure problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Preserve Clinical Workflow
steps.instructions: Confirm that the data-transfer problem does not interfere with active blood processing or patient identification. If electronic transfer is unavailable, use the facility-approved alternate documentation workflow. Do not interrupt active therapy solely to troubleshoot nonessential connectivity. Expected outcome: Patient care and required documentation can continue safely while connectivity is evaluated.

steps.title: 2. Define Which Interface Has Failed
steps.instructions: Determine whether the complaint involves barcode scanning, USB export, wired Ethernet, Wi-Fi, or more than one interface. Ask whether the problem affects every patient or only a particular device, accessory, network location, or destination. Expected outcome: The failure is narrowed to a specific communication method.

steps.title: 3. Verify Basic System Operation
steps.instructions: Confirm the Cell Saver Elite+ starts normally and is not experiencing a broader touchscreen, startup, or shutdown problem. Expected outcome: The device operates normally aside from the reported communication function.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Barcode Scanner or External Accessory
steps.instructions: If barcode scanning is affected, inspect the scanner, cable, connector, and reading surface for damage or contamination. Verify the barcode itself is legible and compatible with the clinical workflow. Use a known-good barcode if available. Expected outcome: The accessory is physically intact and can read a known-good barcode. If replacing or reconnecting the accessory restores scanning, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 5. Inspect USB Media and Connections
steps.instructions: For USB transfer problems, verify the media and external connector are undamaged and fully inserted. If policy permits, test with known-good approved media. Do not connect unapproved or unknown USB devices to clinical equipment. Expected outcome: Approved known-good media is recognized and data transfer functions normally.

steps.title: 6. Inspect Ethernet Cabling and Link Conditions
steps.instructions: For wired connectivity, verify the Ethernet cable is fully seated at both ends and free of visible damage. Test with a known-good approved network cable and known-good network port when available. Expected outcome: The physical network connection is intact. If a cable or port substitution restores connectivity, the issue is resolved.

steps.title: 7. Check Wi-Fi Environment
steps.instructions: For wireless problems, confirm Wi-Fi is expected to be available in the current location and that the issue is not due to unusual distance, shielding, relocation, or a known wireless outage. Do not alter security settings or credentials without authorization. Expected outcome: The device is within the intended wireless environment and no obvious infrastructure limitation is present.

steps.title: 8. Verify Approved Communication Configuration
steps.instructions: Review accessible network or data-transfer settings against approved site documentation. Look for obvious discrepancies without changing addresses, security parameters, destinations, or credentials unless authorized. Expected outcome: Device configuration matches the approved site configuration or a documented discrepancy is identified for correction by authorized personnel.

steps.title: 9. Compare With Other Devices or Network Services
steps.instructions: Determine whether another known-good device can use the same cable, port, Wi-Fi environment, barcode workflow, or destination. This helps separate a Cell Saver Elite+ problem from a facility infrastructure problem. Expected outcome: The failure is isolated to either the equipment, accessory, or external network environment.

steps.title: 10. Verify Data Transfer After Correction
steps.instructions: Perform an approved nonpatient transfer, scan, or connectivity test and confirm the expected destination receives the information correctly. Expected outcome: The complete communication path works as intended. Troubleshooting can stop when repeat testing succeeds.

steps.title: 11. Escalate Persistent Connectivity Problems
steps.instructions: If hardware connections, known-good accessories, approved configuration, and infrastructure checks do not resolve the problem, remove the affected communication function from use and escalate appropriately. If the communication problem compromises required clinical identification, documentation, or device operation, remove the entire system from service. Expected outcome: Unreliable communication is not used clinically until repaired or formally restored.

CCR.Complaint: OR staff reported that the Cell Saver Elite+ would not transfer case data through the wired network connection.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the Ethernet cable damaged near the equipment connector while the network port tested normally.
CCR.Resolution: The cable was replaced with a known-good approved cable, and a test data transfer completed successfully to the expected destination.

helpfulDetails: Transfer result before and after correction

title: Haemonetics Cell Saver Elite+ Cell Salvage System - Centrifuge Will Not Start, Accelerate, or Maintain Speed
description: Addresses centrifuge operation problems caused by loading, cover status, disposable seating, power conditions, obstruction, vibration, or service-level faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Continuity of Care
steps.instructions: Stop reliance on the affected system for active blood processing. Notify the clinical team and establish an alternate blood-management plan before further troubleshooting. Do not troubleshoot an unstable centrifuge while patient blood processing depends on it. Expected outcome: Patient care continues safely without dependence on the malfunctioning centrifuge.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Centrifuge Symptom
steps.instructions: Determine whether the centrifuge does not start at all, starts and immediately stops, accelerates slowly, produces unusual noise or vibration, or appears unable to maintain operating speed. Document any displayed message without assuming its cause. Expected outcome: The centrifuge failure mode is clearly characterized.

steps.title: 3. Verify Normal Power and Startup
steps.instructions: Confirm the system has stable AC power, the power cord is secure, and the equipment starts without unrelated power or startup abnormalities. Test the outlet with appropriate equipment if power quality is in question. Expected outcome: The system has stable power and reaches its normal operating state. If power correction restores centrifuge operation, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Confirm Proper Bowl and Processing-Set Installation
steps.instructions: Inspect the bowl and disposable set for correct seating, alignment, and tubing routing. Ensure no tubing or disposable component interferes with the centrifuge area. Do not operate the centrifuge with questionable seating. Expected outcome: The bowl is seated securely and surrounding components are correctly installed.

steps.title: 5. Verify the Cover Is Fully Closed and Locked
steps.instructions: Confirm the cover closes without obstruction and the system recognizes the locked condition. Do not bypass the cover-lock mechanism. Expected outcome: The system consistently recognizes the secured cover. If proper cover closure restores centrifuge operation, the issue is resolved.

steps.title: 6. Inspect for External Obstruction or Contamination
steps.instructions: With the system powered down as appropriate, inspect accessible centrifuge surroundings for foreign material, dried fluid, damaged disposable components, or anything that could interfere with rotation. Do not manually force or disassemble internal rotating assemblies. Expected outcome: The centrifuge area is visibly clear of external obstruction.

steps.title: 7. Try a Known-Good Compatible Disposable
steps.instructions: If appropriate, install a new known-good bowl and processing set to rule out deformation or improper disposable fit. Expected outcome: The known-good disposable loads correctly and the centrifuge operates normally. If so, the original disposable was the likely external cause.

steps.title: 8. Observe a Nonpatient Centrifuge Start
steps.instructions: Perform an appropriate operational check and observe startup for abnormal scraping, vibration, hesitation, or repeated stopping. Stop the test immediately if mechanical noise, excessive vibration, odor, or other unsafe behavior occurs. Expected outcome: The centrifuge starts and operates smoothly without abnormal mechanical behavior.

steps.title: 9. Verify Stable Operation Through an Appropriate Test Cycle
steps.instructions: If the centrifuge starts normally, verify that it remains stable through an appropriate nonpatient functional sequence using manufacturer-approved procedures. Expected outcome: The centrifuge starts, accelerates, and remains stable without interruption. Troubleshooting can stop if all applicable operational checks pass.

steps.title: 10. Remove From Service if Speed Control Remains Unreliable
steps.instructions: If the centrifuge cannot start or operate consistently after external causes are ruled out, remove the Cell Saver Elite+ from service. Label it Out of Service and send it for qualified bench evaluation. Expected outcome: An unreliable rotating system is prevented from clinical use.

CCR.Complaint: OR staff reported that the centrifuge started briefly and then stopped before blood processing could begin.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the processing bowl incompletely seated in the centrifuge area.
CCR.Resolution: The bowl was reinstalled correctly with a verified compatible processing set, and the centrifuge completed functional testing without abnormal stopping or vibration.

title: Haemonetics Cell Saver Elite+ Cell Salvage System - Cover Will Not Lock or Cover-Lock Indicator Remains Active
description: Addresses cover closure, locking, and cover-status problems caused by obstruction, disposable placement, contamination, misalignment, or damaged external hardware.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Continuity of Care
steps.instructions: Do not continue blood processing with a cover that will not secure or whose status cannot be reliably confirmed. Transfer blood-management needs to an alternate appropriate method before troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Patient care does not depend on the affected system. Continue only after safe continuity of care is established.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Cover Condition
steps.instructions: Determine whether the cover physically will not close, closes but does not lock, opens unexpectedly, or appears mechanically secure while the system still indicates an unlocked condition. Avoid repeatedly forcing or slamming the cover. Expected outcome: The failure is clearly identified as mechanical closure, locking, or status-detection related.

steps.title: 3. Inspect for Disposable Interference
steps.instructions: With processing stopped, inspect the bowl, tubing, and processing set for components protruding into the cover path or preventing full closure. Correct any crossed, pinched, or improperly routed tubing. Expected outcome: No disposable component interferes with cover closure. If correcting the routing allows normal locking and clears the indication, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Cover and Latching Surfaces
steps.instructions: Examine the accessible cover, hinge area, latch contact surfaces, and surrounding housing for cracks, deformation, loose hardware, foreign material, or dried fluid. Do not disassemble the locking mechanism. Expected outcome: The cover and accessible latch surfaces are clean, intact, and aligned. Visible damage requires removal from service.

steps.title: 5. Check Cover Alignment
steps.instructions: Slowly close the cover while observing whether it meets the housing evenly. Look for unusual resistance, side loading, or misalignment before the normal closed position is reached. Do not adjust hinges or internal interlock hardware without approved service guidance. Expected outcome: The cover closes evenly without binding. If simple repositioning of an external obstruction restores proper closure, the issue is resolved.

steps.title: 6. Verify the Processing Bowl Is Fully Seated
steps.instructions: An incompletely seated bowl or disposable can prevent the cover from reaching its intended position. Verify all externally accessible processing-set components are installed correctly. Expected outcome: The disposable and bowl are fully seated and no longer prevent closure. If the cover then locks normally, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 7. Clean Accessible Contact Areas
steps.instructions: If contamination is visible, clean accessible external cover and latch surfaces according to facility and manufacturer-approved cleaning practices. Do not introduce fluid into switches, sensors, or mechanical assemblies. Expected outcome: Contamination is removed and the cover operates smoothly. If the lock indication clears consistently, the issue is resolved.

steps.title: 8. Cycle the Cover Under Nonpatient Conditions
steps.instructions: Close and open the cover several times while observing the mechanical feel and system indication. The state should change consistently without excessive pressure or manipulation. Expected outcome: The cover locks and unlocks predictably, and the displayed status agrees with the physical condition.

steps.title: 9. Perform Functional Verification
steps.instructions: With a correctly loaded compatible disposable, verify the system accepts the closed-cover condition and can proceed through appropriate nonpatient operational checks. Do not return the device to use if the indication is intermittent. Expected outcome: Cover locking and status indication remain stable through repeated testing.

steps.title: 10. Remove From Service if the Condition Persists
steps.instructions: If the cover will not reliably lock or its status remains incorrect despite proper loading and unobstructed closure, remove the unit from service. Label it Out of Service and send it for qualified bench evaluation. Expected outcome: A system with an unreliable safety-related cover condition is kept out of clinical use.

CCR.Complaint: Perfusion staff reported that the centrifuge cover would close but the cover-lock indication remained active.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a section of disposable tubing trapped along the cover edge and preventing complete closure.
CCR.Resolution: The tubing was correctly repositioned, the cover locked normally, and repeated functional testing confirmed stable cover-status indication.

title: Haemonetics Cell Saver Elite+ Cell Salvage System - Processing Set, Bowl, or Tubing Will Not Load Correctly
description: Addresses disposable processing-set, centrifuge-bowl, and tubing installation problems caused by incorrect seating, routing, damaged components, or incompatible disposables.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Continuity of Care
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot a cell salvage system while the patient depends on unreliable blood recovery or reinfusion capability. Notify the clinical team and establish an alternate blood-management plan before removing the system from active use. If recovered blood is already present, maintain appropriate handling and disposition according to facility policy and clinical direction. Expected outcome: Patient care continues safely without dependence on the malfunctioning Cell Saver Elite+. If alternate support is established, continue troubleshooting.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Loading Problem
steps.instructions: Ask staff to describe where installation fails: initial set placement, bowl seating, tubing routing, pump-segment loading, cover closure, or recognition after installation. Inspect the system without forcing any disposable component into position. Expected outcome: The loading failure is reproduced or clearly localized. If correct installation resolves the complaint and the system recognizes the disposable normally, troubleshooting can stop after functional verification.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Correct Processing Set Is Being Used
steps.instructions: Confirm the disposable set is appropriate for the Cell Saver Elite+ and is within its usable packaging condition. Inspect for damaged packaging, bent components, deformation, contamination, or evidence that the set was previously opened or improperly stored. Do not modify a disposable to make it fit. Expected outcome: A correct, undamaged processing set is available. If replacing an obviously damaged or incorrect set restores normal loading, the issue is resolved.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Bowl and Mechanical Seating Areas
steps.instructions: With the system safely stopped, inspect accessible bowl-retaining surfaces and mounting areas for debris, dried fluid, foreign material, or obstruction. Verify the bowl is oriented and seated without tilting or excessive resistance. Do not force the bowl into the centrifuge mechanism. Expected outcome: The bowl seats fully and evenly without obstruction. If normal seating restores operation, troubleshooting can stop after completing the normal startup checks.

steps.title: 5. Inspect External Tubing Routing
steps.instructions: Trace the disposable tubing through all externally accessible routing points. Look for crossed tubing, twists, kinks, tubing trapped beneath another component, or tubing positioned where it prevents proper cover closure. Correct routing using approved manufacturer documentation when needed. Expected outcome: Tubing follows the intended path without kinks, trapping, or interference. If the system then accepts the set normally, the issue is resolved.

steps.title: 6. Check Pump-Segment Placement
steps.instructions: Inspect the disposable tubing segment that interfaces with the pump mechanism. Verify it is not twisted, stretched, pinched, or partially seated. Do not operate the pump against improperly loaded tubing. Expected outcome: The pump tubing is securely and evenly positioned. If correcting placement restores normal set loading and pump operation, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 7. Inspect Accessible Latches, Guides, and Retainers
steps.instructions: Inspect external guides, retaining features, doors, and latching surfaces involved in disposable installation. Look for cracks, bent parts, looseness, contamination, or obvious mechanical damage. Do not attempt internal mechanical adjustment or disassembly. Expected outcome: All accessible retaining components move normally and show no damage. An obviously damaged retaining mechanism requires removal from service and repair evaluation.

steps.title: 8. Perform a Known-Good Disposable Comparison
steps.instructions: If permitted and practical, install a new known-good compatible processing set. Compare how it seats and routes with the set involved in the complaint. Do not reuse a potentially compromised disposable for patient care. Expected outcome: The known-good set loads normally. If so, the original disposable was the likely external cause and troubleshooting can stop after documenting the finding.

steps.title: 9. Verify Normal System Recognition and Operation
steps.instructions: After installation, confirm the system accepts the disposable arrangement, closes normally, and completes applicable startup or operational checks without abnormal noise, binding, or repeated loading indications. Do not proceed to clinical use if installation remains questionable. Expected outcome: The Cell Saver Elite+ recognizes the installed components and operates normally through an appropriate nonpatient functional verification.

steps.title: 10. Remove From Service if Loading Remains Unreliable
steps.instructions: If multiple correctly installed compatible sets will not load, seat, or remain secured, remove the system from service. Label it Out of Service and send it for bench evaluation using approved manufacturer documentation and appropriate test equipment. Expected outcome: An unresolved or mechanically unreliable unit is prevented from returning to clinical use.

CCR.Complaint: OR staff reported that the processing bowl would not seat correctly and the Cell Saver Elite+ could not be prepared for use.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the disposable tubing crossed beneath the bowl area and preventing full seating.
CCR.Resolution: Tubing was rerouted correctly, the bowl seated normally, and the system completed functional verification without further loading problems.

helpfulDetails: System indication before and after correction

title: Haemonetics Cell Saver Elite+ Cell Salvage System - Pump Will Not Turn or Blood Flow Is Intermittent
description: Addresses pump and flow interruptions caused by tubing loading, kinks, clamps, disposable problems, obstruction, power issues, or pump-drive faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Continuity of Care
steps.instructions: If blood collection or processing is unreliable, notify the clinical team and establish an alternate blood-management plan. Do not continue using a system with unpredictable blood flow. Expected outcome: Patient care continues without relying on intermittent Cell Saver Elite+ flow.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Pump or Flow Problem
steps.instructions: Determine whether the pump does not rotate, rotates without moving fluid, starts and stops intermittently, or produces irregular flow. Observe the condition without allowing continued operation against a visibly obstructed line. Expected outcome: The complaint is identified as a pump-motion, tubing-loading, or fluid-path issue.

steps.title: 3. Verify Power and Overall System State
steps.instructions: Confirm stable AC power, complete startup, and absence of unrelated shutdown or cover conditions preventing normal operation. Expected outcome: The system is powered normally and otherwise ready to operate. If restoring power or startup status restores pump operation, the issue is resolved.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Pump Tubing Placement
steps.instructions: Examine the disposable tubing where it interfaces with the pump. Look for partial loading, twisting, flattening, stretching, or tubing positioned outside the intended track. Do not operate the pump against incorrectly seated tubing. Expected outcome: The pump segment is correctly loaded and evenly seated. If correcting it restores reliable flow, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 5. Trace the External Fluid Path
steps.instructions: Inspect the blood path for closed clamps, kinked tubing, compressed tubing, collapsed sections, or tubing trapped under equipment or disposables. Verify associated connections are fully seated. Expected outcome: The external fluid path is open and unobstructed. If correcting an obstruction restores flow, the issue is resolved.

steps.title: 6. Inspect the Disposable for Damage or Clotting
steps.instructions: Look for visible clot, debris, collapsed tubing, damaged connectors, or other disposable conditions that could restrict blood movement. Do not attempt to salvage or reuse a compromised disposable. Expected outcome: The disposable path appears patent and intact. A compromised disposable is replaced according to clinical and facility procedures.

steps.title: 7. Check Accessible Pump Components
steps.instructions: With the device safely stopped, inspect accessible pump surfaces for contamination, foreign material, or damage that could interfere with tubing contact. Do not dismantle the pump assembly. Expected outcome: The accessible pump area is clean and unobstructed.

steps.title: 8. Perform a Known-Good Disposable Test
steps.instructions: When clinically appropriate and permitted, test the system with a new compatible processing set to distinguish a disposable problem from an equipment problem. Expected outcome: Reliable pump operation with a known-good set indicates the original disposable or tubing configuration was the likely cause.

steps.title: 9. Perform Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Under nonpatient conditions, verify consistent pump rotation and fluid movement through an appropriate test configuration. Observe for slipping, irregular motion, noise, or stopping. Expected outcome: Pump operation and flow remain stable. If testing is normal, troubleshooting can stop and the device may proceed through required return-to-service checks.

steps.title: 10. Remove From Service if Pump Operation Is Unreliable
steps.instructions: If the pump remains intermittent or fails to rotate after external causes are ruled out, remove the system from service. Label it Out of Service and refer it for bench evaluation. Expected outcome: A system incapable of reliable blood movement is not returned to patient care.

CCR.Complaint: Surgical staff reported intermittent blood flow even though the pump appeared to start normally.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the pump tubing segment twisted and only partially seated in the pump track.
CCR.Resolution: The tubing was correctly reseated, and repeated functional testing confirmed stable pump rotation and continuous fluid movement.

title: Haemonetics Cell Saver Elite+ Cell Salvage System - Reservoir Level, Bowl Level, or Optical Sensor Error
description: Addresses incorrect fluid-level or optical detection caused by disposable placement, contamination, foam, tubing position, damaged disposables, or sensor-related faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Continuity of Care
steps.instructions: Do not continue processing if the system cannot reliably determine blood or fluid level. Establish an alternate blood-management plan before troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Patient care continues safely without relying on uncertain level detection.

steps.title: 2. Record the Exact Indication and Operating Condition
steps.instructions: Document the displayed message or abnormal level behavior and note whether it occurs at startup, during filling, processing, washing, or empty conditions. Compare the indicated state with the visible condition of the disposable. Expected outcome: The discrepancy is clearly defined and can be correlated with a particular disposable or operating state.

steps.title: 3. Inspect Reservoir and Bowl Installation
steps.instructions: Verify the reservoir, bowl, and associated disposable components are seated in the correct accessible positions without tilting, incomplete insertion, or interference. Expected outcome: Disposable components are physically positioned as intended. If reseating corrects the indication, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Sensor Viewing Areas for Contamination
steps.instructions: Examine externally accessible optical or level-sensing windows and adjacent disposable surfaces for blood residue, condensation, labels, tape, debris, or other material that could obstruct sensing. Clean only according to approved manufacturer and facility procedures. Expected outcome: Sensor viewing areas are clean and unobstructed.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Disposable for Clouding, Damage, or Deformation
steps.instructions: Look for scratches, discoloration, deformation, trapped material, or damage in areas where the system observes fluid levels. Do not modify the disposable. Expected outcome: The disposable presents a clear and properly positioned sensing surface.

steps.title: 6. Check for Foam, Bubbles, or Irregular Fluid Conditions
steps.instructions: Observe whether excessive foam, air, or unusual fluid distribution is present near the level-sensing area. These conditions can alter optical detection even when the sensor hardware is functioning. Address the underlying external fluid-path cause rather than altering system calibration. Expected outcome: The fluid interface appears stable and consistent with normal processing conditions.

steps.title: 7. Verify Tubing and Flow Conditions
steps.instructions: Confirm tubing is not kinked, obstructed, or incorrectly routed in a way that causes abnormal reservoir or bowl filling. Expected outcome: Fluid moves predictably through the disposable path without abnormal filling patterns.

steps.title: 8. Test With a Known-Good Compatible Disposable
steps.instructions: If practical, use a known-good compatible processing set or relevant disposable component to determine whether the indication follows the original set. Expected outcome: Correct level detection with a known-good disposable indicates the original disposable was the likely cause.

steps.title: 9. Perform Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Under nonpatient conditions, observe level indications through an appropriate operational sequence. Verify displayed status agrees with the actual disposable condition. Do not enter unauthorized calibration or sensor-adjustment modes. Expected outcome: Level and optical indications remain accurate and stable. Troubleshooting can stop if repeated verification is successful.

steps.title: 10. Remove From Service if Detection Remains Incorrect
steps.instructions: If correct disposable positioning, clean sensing areas, normal fluid conditions, and known-good components do not restore reliable detection, remove the system from service. Expected outcome: Equipment with unreliable fluid-level detection is labeled Out of Service and referred for bench evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: OR staff reported repeated bowl-level indications even though the disposable appeared to be filling normally.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found dried residue on an accessible optical sensing surface adjacent to the bowl.
CCR.Resolution: The surface was cleaned using approved methods, and repeated functional testing confirmed stable level detection through the test cycle.

title: Haemonetics Cell Saver Elite+ Cell Salvage System - Touchscreen, Beacon, Startup, or Unexpected Shutdown
description: Addresses control, indicator, startup, and shutdown problems caused by power, connections, contamination, environmental conditions, or internal service-level faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Continuity of Care
steps.instructions: If the Cell Saver Elite+ becomes unresponsive, shuts down unexpectedly, or cannot reliably display or indicate operating status, stop depending on it for blood processing. Notify the clinical team and establish an alternate blood-management plan. Expected outcome: Patient care continues safely without dependence on unreliable equipment.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the touchscreen is unresponsive, the beacon does not indicate normally, the unit will not complete startup, or the system unexpectedly powers off or restarts. Document what was displayed immediately before the problem occurred. Expected outcome: The complaint is clearly characterized and, when possible, reproduced under safe nonpatient conditions.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the AC Power Connection
steps.instructions: Verify the power cord is fully seated at the equipment and receptacle. Inspect the cord and plug for cuts, bent contacts, looseness, discoloration, or other damage. Expected outcome: The AC connection is secure and undamaged. If restoring a loose connection resolves the issue, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Test the Power Source
steps.instructions: Use appropriate test equipment or a known-good receptacle to rule out a defective outlet, switched receptacle, loose power strip, or facility power problem. Avoid using unapproved extension cords or power adapters. Expected outcome: The Cell Saver Elite+ receives stable facility power.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Touchscreen and Controls
steps.instructions: Check the touchscreen and accessible control surfaces for fluid, residue, protective coverings, labels, or other material that could interfere with touch response. Clean only with approved methods. Expected outcome: The touchscreen surface is clean and unobstructed. If cleaning restores normal response, the issue is resolved after functional verification.

steps.title: 6. Check for Physical Damage
steps.instructions: Inspect the display, touchscreen, housing, beacon, switches, connectors, and power cord for cracks, impact damage, liquid intrusion, or loose components. If liquid intrusion, burning odor, excessive heat, or electrical damage is suspected, stop testing immediately. Expected outcome: No unsafe physical condition is present. Any significant damage requires immediate removal from service.

steps.title: 7. Evaluate Environmental Conditions
steps.instructions: Determine whether the shutdown or control problem occurred after transport, impact, fluid exposure, unusual heat, blocked ventilation, or connection to questionable power. Inspect accessible ventilation openings for external blockage. Expected outcome: The equipment is operating in a suitable environment with unobstructed ventilation and stable power.

steps.title: 8. Perform a Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: When appropriate and no patient depends on the system, shut the unit down normally, allow the shutdown to complete, and restart it. Do not repeatedly power-cycle a unit that continuously fails startup or produces abnormal symptoms. Expected outcome: The system completes startup and all normal controls and indicators become available.

steps.title: 9. Verify Touchscreen and Beacon Operation
steps.instructions: Under nonpatient conditions, confirm the touchscreen responds consistently across the functions needed for normal operation and that the beacon or external status indication behaves consistently with system state. Do not enter restricted service modes. Expected outcome: Controls and indicators operate reliably without intermittent loss of response.

steps.title: 10. Observe for Unexpected Shutdown
steps.instructions: Allow the device to remain powered and perform an appropriate functional sequence while monitoring for rebooting, power loss, overheating, unusual odor, or display failure. Expected outcome: The system remains powered and stable through the verification period. If operation remains normal, troubleshooting can stop after completing required return-to-service testing.

steps.title: 11. Remove From Service if the Problem Recurs
steps.instructions: Any recurring unexpected shutdown, unreliable touchscreen, failed startup, or inconsistent critical indication is sufficient reason to remove the system from service. Expected outcome: The device is labeled Out of Service and referred for qualified bench evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: OR staff reported that the Cell Saver Elite+ unexpectedly shut down during setup and would restart when the power cord was moved.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found visible damage and intermittent continuity at the external power cord near the equipment connector.
CCR.Resolution: The damaged cord was replaced with an approved replacement, and extended functional testing confirmed stable startup, touchscreen operation, indicators, and continuous power.

title: Haemonetics Cell Saver Elite+ Cell Salvage System - Vacuum Is Low, Unstable, or Unavailable
description: Addresses absent or unstable vacuum caused by leaks, loose tubing, blocked filters or disposables, connection errors, external setup, or vacuum-system faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Continuity of Care
steps.instructions: If adequate surgical suction or blood recovery cannot be maintained, notify the clinical team and establish alternate suction before troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Necessary suction remains available without depending on the affected Cell Saver Elite+.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Vacuum Symptom
steps.instructions: Determine whether vacuum is completely absent, weak, intermittent, slow to develop, or drops under load. Identify whether the problem affects the complete aspiration system or only one attached circuit. Expected outcome: The vacuum problem is clearly characterized and localized as far as possible.

steps.title: 3. Verify System Power and Operating State
steps.instructions: Confirm stable AC power and normal system startup. Ensure no unrelated condition is preventing the system from enabling vacuum operation. Expected outcome: The system has stable power and is otherwise operating normally.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Vacuum and Aspiration Connections
steps.instructions: Check all accessible tubing and fittings associated with the vacuum path for loose connections, disconnected tubing, cracked fittings, or improperly seated ports. Expected outcome: All external vacuum connections are secure. If correcting a loose connection restores vacuum, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Tubing for Leaks or Collapse
steps.instructions: Trace the line for cracks, punctures, kinks, compression, and collapsed sections. Pay particular attention to points where tubing bends around equipment or connects to disposable components. Expected outcome: The tubing is intact and mechanically open.

steps.title: 6. Inspect Disposable Components for Restriction
steps.instructions: Check relevant externally accessible filters, reservoirs, connectors, and disposable pathways for visible obstruction, fluid saturation, clotting, or damage. Replace compromised disposables rather than attempting to clean or reuse them. Expected outcome: The disposable vacuum path is free of obvious restriction.

steps.title: 7. Verify Reservoir and Port Sealing
steps.instructions: Inspect reservoir connections and unused ports for proper closure or sealing according to the intended setup. An open or poorly sealed port can reduce available vacuum. Expected outcome: The reservoir system is sealed appropriately. If correcting a port or connection stabilizes vacuum, the issue is resolved.

steps.title: 8. Compare With a Known-Good Tubing or Disposable Setup
steps.instructions: If practical, connect a known-good compatible vacuum or aspiration setup to determine whether the vacuum problem follows the original disposable circuit. Expected outcome: Normal vacuum with a known-good setup indicates the original disposable path was the likely external cause.

steps.title: 9. Perform a Nonpatient Vacuum Verification
steps.instructions: Using an appropriate test configuration, confirm that vacuum develops and remains stable under a reasonable functional load. Do not rely solely on sound or subjective feel. Expected outcome: Vacuum is consistently available and stable. Troubleshooting can stop if repeated verification is successful.

steps.title: 10. Remove From Service if Vacuum Remains Unreliable
steps.instructions: If all accessible tubing, ports, seals, disposable components, and power conditions are verified but vacuum remains low or unstable, remove the system from service. Expected outcome: The unit is labeled Out of Service and referred for qualified evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: OR staff reported that vacuum was weak and fluctuated during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an aspiration tubing connection partially disengaged from the reservoir port.
CCR.Resolution: The connection was reseated securely, and nonpatient testing confirmed stable vacuum throughout repeated operation.

title: Haemonetics Cell Saver Elite+ Cell Salvage System - Wash Cycle, Recentrifuge, or Final Cycle Will Not Complete
description: Addresses incomplete processing cycles caused by disposable flow restrictions, insufficient fluids, tubing problems, centrifuge interruptions, sensor conditions, or system faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Continuity of Care
steps.instructions: Do not rely on incompletely processed blood for reinfusion. Notify the clinical team and maintain an alternate blood-management plan while the cause is evaluated. Handle any partially processed blood according to clinical policy and manufacturer instructions. Expected outcome: Patient care continues without dependence on an incomplete or uncertain processing cycle.

steps.title: 2. Identify the Exact Cycle and Stopping Point
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem occurs during wash, recentrifuge, final processing, or another transition. Record any displayed message and what the system was doing immediately before the cycle stopped. Expected outcome: The failure is tied to a specific stage and repeatable condition.

steps.title: 3. Verify Stable Power
steps.instructions: Confirm AC power is secure and the system has not experienced a power interruption, loose plug, damaged cord, or unexpected shutdown. Expected outcome: Stable power is available throughout the processing cycle. If correcting the power source allows a complete cycle, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Check Required External Fluids and Containers
steps.instructions: Inspect all applicable external fluid bags, collection containers, and drainage destinations required for the cycle. Look for empty sources, full receiving containers, closed clamps, or improper connections. Expected outcome: Required fluids and collection pathways are available and correctly connected.

steps.title: 5. Trace the Disposable Fluid Path
steps.instructions: Inspect tubing for kinks, closed clamps, collapsed sections, improper routing, air, or visible obstruction. Verify connectors are fully seated. Expected outcome: The disposable path is open and properly routed. If correcting an obstruction allows the cycle to complete, the issue is resolved.

steps.title: 6. Verify Bowl and Reservoir Seating
steps.instructions: Confirm the bowl and reservoir remain securely installed and have not shifted during operation. Expected outcome: Disposable components remain properly positioned throughout the cycle.

steps.title: 7. Check for Related Centrifuge or Pump Instability
steps.instructions: Observe whether the processing interruption coincides with abnormal centrifuge noise, pump stopping, unstable flow, or another subsystem problem. Do not continue testing if abnormal mechanical behavior is present. Expected outcome: Pump and centrifuge operation remain stable through the cycle.

steps.title: 8. Inspect Level and Optical Sensing Conditions
steps.instructions: Look for foam, bubbles, contamination, or disposable positioning that could prevent the system from recognizing required fluid transitions. Expected outcome: External sensing conditions are clear and consistent with proper processing.

steps.title: 9. Test With a Known-Good Compatible Processing Set
steps.instructions: When appropriate, use a known-good disposable set to determine whether the incomplete cycle follows the original disposable. Expected outcome: A complete cycle with a known-good set identifies the original disposable or setup as the likely cause.

steps.title: 10. Perform a Complete Nonpatient Functional Cycle
steps.instructions: After correcting any external cause, run an appropriate test sequence through completion and verify that all relevant steps advance normally without manual intervention or repeated faults. Expected outcome: The cycle completes normally. Troubleshooting can stop when the system performs consistently and passes applicable return-to-service checks.

steps.title: 11. Remove From Service if a Cycle Still Cannot Complete
steps.instructions: If the system repeatedly fails to complete processing after external conditions are ruled out, remove it from service. Expected outcome: The unit is labeled Out of Service and sent for qualified bench evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: OR staff reported that the wash cycle repeatedly stopped before completing.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the wash-fluid tubing kinked beneath the equipment cart and restricting flow.
CCR.Resolution: The tubing was repositioned, and the Cell Saver Elite+ subsequently completed a full functional processing cycle without interruption.
